title: The 5 Longest Pregnancies on Earth, Ranked (#1 Is Not a Mammal)

scenes.text: The five longest pregnancies on Earth. Number one outlasts every elephant, and it isn't even a mammal.

scenes.label: Giraffe · 15 months
scenes.text: Number five: the giraffe. Around fifteen months before the calf arrives, longer than a whole year.

scenes.label: Orca · 17 months
scenes.text: Number four: the orca. Around seventeen months, a year and a half of pregnancy.

scenes.label: African elephant · 22 months
scenes.text: Number three: the African elephant. Twenty-two months, almost two full years.

scenes.label: Alpine salamander · 3 years
scenes.text: Number two: the alpine salamander, high in the mountains. Up to three years, depending on how cold it is.

scenes.label: Frilled shark · 3.5 years
scenes.text: Number one: the frilled shark. Estimates run up to three and a half years, the longest pregnancy known.

description:
The five longest pregnancies on Earth, ranked by length.
The giraffe carries for around 15 months, the orca around 17, and the African elephant 22. Alpine salamanders in cold mountain habitats can carry for up to 3 years, and the frilled shark is estimated at up to 3.5 years, though that figure is uncertain.
Which one surprised you most?
first_comment: Frilled shark gestation is estimated, not directly measured. Which would you have put at number one, and what should we rank next?
